questions.q: Which capability does Slurm provide natively that Kubernetes needs an add-on (like Volcano) to get?
options: Container image management
Gang scheduling and GPU-aware allocation
The ability to run any workload at all
DNS resolution between nodes
questions.explain: Slurm was purpose-built for batch HPC workloads, so gang scheduling and GPU-aware allocation (--gres=gpu:N) are native. Kubernetes' scheduler was built service-first and needs Volcano to add equivalent gang scheduling.

questions.q: What is the main operational advantage Kubernetes offers Solara AI specifically, beyond raw scheduling features?
options: It is the only platform capable of running GPU workloads
Solara already runs other infrastructure on Kubernetes, so training jobs share the same tooling, monitoring, and operational knowledge as the rest of the platform
Kubernetes guarantees faster model convergence
Kubernetes eliminates the need for any scheduler at all
questions.explain: The value isn't a unique scheduling feature — it's that Kubernetes is already the platform Solara's team operates, so training reuses existing tooling, monitoring, and runbooks instead of adding a second platform.

questions.q: Why might a research team at Solara AI prefer submitting an sbatch script over writing a PyTorchJob manifest for a quick experiment?
options: PyTorchJob manifests cannot request GPUs
sbatch scripts are faster to write for researchers already familiar with HPC/academic cluster conventions, and Slurm's batch-job model maps directly onto a quick experimental run
Slurm is the only system that supports PyTorch
Kubernetes requires a paid license to submit any job
questions.explain: Many researchers come from academic HPC backgrounds where Slurm and sbatch are already familiar tools, making it quicker to iterate on experiments compared to authoring a PyTorchJob CRD manifest.

questions.q: According to the comparison, what is the main operational cost of adopting Slurm for a team that also runs other non-training infrastructure?
options: Slurm cannot schedule any job larger than one node
Slurm has no concept of priority or queues
Slurm doesn't provide the broader ecosystem (service discovery, ingress, autoscaling integrations) Kubernetes offers, so it becomes a second platform to operate alongside Kubernetes
Slurm requires every job to run as root
questions.explain: Slurm's narrow focus on batch HPC jobs means a team already running services on Kubernetes would need to operate and secure an entirely separate platform for anything Slurm doesn't cover.

questions.q: What is Solara AI's actual resolution to the Kubernetes-vs-Slurm question?
options: They dropped Kubernetes entirely in favor of Slurm
They dropped Slurm entirely in favor of Kubernetes
They run both — Kubernetes with the Training Operator and Volcano for production runs, Slurm for research-team experimentation — matching each tool to the team using it
They alternate platforms every month regardless of workload
questions.explain: Solara AI uses Kubernetes as the primary path for production training because the platform team already operates it, while keeping Slurm available for researchers who iterate faster with sbatch — running both deliberately rather than picking one.
